title: Local pair correlations and network geometry govern collective oscillations in nonreciprocal Ising networks
authors: Zihua Liu, Xudong Wu, Liantuan Xiao
abstract: Nonreciprocal many-body dynamics can develop a swap phase characterized by spontaneous global oscillations far from equilibrium. To determine how local nonreciprocal interactions predict global oscillations and how broadly this prediction applies, we compare mean-field theory, independent-node theory, and nearest-neighbor spin-coupling theory for a two-spin nonreciprocal Ising model on networks of fixed coordination number (\(z=4\)). Nearest-neighbor spin-coupling theory retains nine independent joint edge probabilities. Monte Carlo benchmarks show that it predicts the oscillation amplitude, angular momentum, and period on edge-swapped networks with a 2.1\% aggregate mean absolute relative error. We then extend the square lattice to degree-preserving edge-swapped networks and find sharply different behavior. With increasing system size, the oscillation amplitude and angular momentum decay strongly on the periodic square lattice but remain nearly size independent on edge-swapped networks. These results show that identical local parameters do not determine the macroscopic phase. The contrasting finite-size trends identify network geometry as a key determinant of collective oscillations at fixed local interaction parameters.
summary: This work investigates collective oscillations in nonreciprocal Ising spin networks, comparing theoretical approximations against detailed Monte Carlo simulations. The key finding is that while local interaction parameters are crucial, the macroscopic oscillatory behavior is fundamentally dictated by the network's geometry, as demonstrated by contrasting results on periodic versus edge-swapped lattices.
main_problem: The study aims to determine how local nonreciprocal interactions predict global collective oscillations in nonreciprocal Ising networks, and whether network geometry is the key determinant of these oscillations.
main_result: The paper finds that while local theories can predict oscillations on edge-swapped networks, the macroscopic behavior (amplitude and angular momentum) strongly depends on the underlying network geometry, showing a clear difference between periodic lattices and swapped ones.
method: The authors compare three theoretical approximations (Mean-Field, Independent-Node, Nearest-Neighbor Spin-Coupling) against extensive Monte Carlo simulations on different network topologies.
model_or_system: The system is a two-spin nonreciprocal Ising model defined on a connected undirected network, featuring nonreciprocal Glauber dynamics. The model is analyzed on both periodic square lattices and degree-preserving edge-swapped networks.
key_observables: Oscillation amplitude ($R_{rms}$), angular momentum ($L$), and period ($T$) are the primary global diagnostics used to characterize the collective dynamics.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the coupling strengths ($ eta J,  eta K^+,  eta K^-$), the coordination number ($z=4$), system size ($L$), and the edge-swapping intensity ($f$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing theoretical closures (MF, ID, NSC) against the full, non-equilibrium dynamics simulated via Monte Carlo methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup, the comparison of theoretical predictions vs. MC results for $R_{rms}, L, T$ across different couplings, and finite-size scaling tests showing the divergence of behavior between square lattices and edge-swapped networks.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model and comparing local theories (MF, ID, NSC) against MC simulations. It then performs finite-size scaling tests by comparing results on periodic lattices versus edge-swapped networks to isolate the role of geometry.
why_interesting: The focus on non-equilibrium dynamics, collective oscillations, and the explicit comparison of local correlation approximations (NSC) to global behavior is highly relevant to open quantum systems and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Nonreciprocal model and degree-preserving edge swapping. (a) Each site carries one binary spin from species A and one from species B. The responses B →A and A →B are asymmetric. (b) Local view of the periodic square lattice. Spins of the same species interact reciprocally with strength J along undirected edges, and the full network has coordination number z = 4. (c) A valid double-edge swap reconnects two removed edges crosswise. It changes short cycles and long-range connections while preserving the coordination number of every node. Magenta curves show the new edges and dotted lines show the removed edges.

Figure 5 uses two additional L = 208, N = 43264, trajectories. Each trajectory is thermalized for 3000 MCS and prescanned for 640 MCS at intervals of 2 MCS. A frame is selected near a prespecified global phase, then the microscopic state is reproduced deterministically with the same network and dynamical seeds.

Figure 2: Predictions of global oscillation characteristics by the local theories. All panels use βK+ = 0, βK−= 0.50, z = 4, and τ = 1. (a) Phase-plane trajectories at βJ = 0.50. MF converges to the black static ordered point. ID, BG, and NSC produce limit cycles, with ID markedly overestimating the amplitude. (b) Oscillation amplitude. (c) Angular momentum calculated at ∆t = 2τ. (d) Period. The period is comparatively insensitive to the local information retained by the theories. Theory curves in panels (b)–(d) use 201 coupling values. The lower axes show the relative difference between BG and NSC, defined as 100(XBG −XNSC)/XNSC. The gray zero line is a guide to the eye.

Figure 3: Finite-size test at βJ = 0.50, βK+ = 0, βK−= 0.50, and z = 4. (a,b) Representative L = 32 magnetization trajectories over 180 MCS. (c) Oscillation amplitude. (d) Angular momentum. (e) Period obtained from filtered upward crossings of mA = 0. Symbols represent nine simulated sizes. Error bars for edge-swapped networks are standard errors over four independent networks. Error bars for the square lattice are obtained from four independent dynamical batches on the same periodic topology. Dotted lines are a + b/N fits. Horizontal solid lines show the NSC prediction at βJ = 0.50.

Figure 4: Coupling scan at L = 48, βK+ = 0, βK−= 0.50, and z = 4. (a) Oscillation amplitude. (b) Angular momentum calculated at ∆t = 2τ. (c) Effective upward crossing period. Symbols show Monte Carlo results. Error bars are standard errors across independent networks for f > 0 and independent dynamical batches for the square lattice. The two edge-swapped series are displaced by ±0.00065 along the βJ axis for visibility only. Each theoretical line contains 201 independent ODE solutions. The theory curves represent NSC, BG, and ID. For the square lattice, T denotes an effective crossing period from low-amplitude fluctuations.
